newsitem.title: ITALY: Cariverona to sell stake in Ambroveneto.
newsitem.headline: Cariverona to sell stake in Ambroveneto.

text.p: Italian savings bank Cassa di Risparmio di Verona (Cariverona) said it had given its chairman a mandate to sell a 12.62 percent stake in Banco Ambrosiano Veneto (Ambroveneto).
Cariverona said in a statement issued after a board meeting: "The board deemed the presence in the shareholder structure of Ambroveneto was no longer strategic.

"As a result the board has given a wide mandate to the chairman Paolo Biasi to proceed, in the best way and over the best time-frame, with the sale of the 12.62 percent stake in Ambroveneto which Cariverona has in its portfolio," it said.

Ambroveneto shares were 2.68 percent up on the day at 4,820 lire per ordinary share, higher than the morning session when they were 1.6 percent up. The bourse is generally weaker with the all-share Mibtel index, 0.87 percent down on the day.
Cariverona is one of the shareholders in a shareholder syndicate in Ambroveneto.

Ambroveneto is currently in negotiations to merge with Italy's largest savings bank Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde (Cariplo). The merger, if it goes ahead, will create the country's second biggest bank in asset terms after San Paolo di Torino.
